His most famous work is the 'Kitab al-Tarikh' or 'The Book of History', which covers the history of the Islamic world from the time of the Prophet Muhammad to the 10th century. Al-Ragheib's history is considered an important source for the study of Islamic history during this period.

historical_references.context: Saint Ragheed Al-Tabarani, also known as Saint Raphael, was a Christian monk and bishop in Syria. He is said to have lived during the 9th century and was martyred during the Islamic conquest of Syria. According to tradition, Ragheed was killed by Muslim soldiers for refusing to renounce his Christian faith. He is venerated as a saint in the Eastern Orthodox and Roman Catholic Churches, and his feast day is celebrated on October 26.

modern_usage.modern_context: Ragheed is a modern Arabic name of Iraqi descent, derived from the ancient name Al-Rihid, which means 'the sharp-tongued'. However, in contemporary usage, Ragheed is most commonly associated with Ragheed Ganni, a Christian Chaldean priest from Mosul, Iraq, who was brutally murdered by militant extremists in 2007. His death was a significant event in the ongoing persecution of Christians and other religious minorities in Iraq and the Middle East. Ragheed's martyrdom sparked global outrage, leading to numerous campaigns and initiatives focused on Christian activism, human rights, and the protection of religious freedom. His legacy lives on through social media, news media, and academic research, as a symbol of courage and sacrifice in the face of religious intolerance.
